extracted.intended_audience: State health agencies, Marketplace exchanges, issuers, agents/brokers/web-brokers, and other stakeholders responding to an HHS proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and evaluating the regulatory standards, requirements, and impact assumptions in a proposed HHS rule concerning Exchange operations, eligibility, verification, marketing, and related program integrity measures under the Affordable Care Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: State defrayal requirement for State‑required benefits meeting four conjunctive elements (§155.170(a)(1)(i)-(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any State-required benefit that fulfills the four proposed conjunctive elements at proposed §155.170(a)(1)(i) through (iv) would require defrayal, regardless of whether the benefit is included in the State's EHB-benchmark plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that States that had sought benchmark changes to add State-required benefits without defrayal may be frustrated; States that stopped defraying beginning PY 2025 could see decreases in the percentage of premium attributable to EHB for APTC calculation if required to defray starting PY 2027. States may avoid defrayal for benefits already in the EHB-benchmark by repealing the State requirement as applicable to QHPs. HHS solicits comment on administrative costs, estimates of defrayal scale, issuer plan-design modifications, and on delaying effective date to PY 2028 given legislative/filing timing variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandate to use HHS‑approved consumer consent form for eligibility application review (§155.220(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents, brokers, and web-brokers would be required to use the HHS‑approved and ‑created consumer consent form to meet eligibility application review requirements and consent documentation requirements, eliminating broader current allowances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goal: reduce confusion and ensure objective standards protecting consumers and improving HHS investigative ability. Acknowledges impacts on entities that relied on phone recordings or texts; consumers interacting by phone may find it burdensome. Notes the form underwent readability analysis. Estimates an annual cost of $96,694,640 beginning in PY 2027. HHS seeks comments on these impact estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing standards of conduct and prohibition on misleading marketing (§155.220(j)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a new standards of conduct section listing prohibited marketing practices, providing HHS audit authority, and holding agents/brokers/web-brokers responsible for marketing by downstream entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Would provide instructive language to create compliant Exchange marketing, allow HHS to review marketing materials and pursue compliance actions, and prevent deflection of responsibility to third parties. Estimated burden for responding to HHS regarding misleading marketing is $1,392.96 beginning in 2027. Solicits comment on impact estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of the vendor program (§155.222)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove vendor program requirements that allowed training and information verification to be provided by HHS‑approved vendors, permitting HHS to discontinue the vendor program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: lack of utilization and dwindling vendor interest. Agents/brokers can continue annual training and verification via MLMS at no cost. Anticipated government savings approximately $300,000 per plan year beginning 2027. HHS does not anticipate substantial impacts to agents/brokers or potential vendors but seeks comments on impact estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limiting APTC eligibility to 'eligible noncitizens' (§§155.20, 155.305(f)(1), 155.320)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals receiving APTC who are lawfully present noncitizens but not 'eligible noncitizens' would become ineligible for APTC and income‑based CSRs beginning in PY 2027 under the referenced legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS estimates 1,227,000 individuals impacted, reducing annual APTC expenditures by $9,672,048,360 beginning 2027. Anticipates system update costs ($15,810,185 in PY 2026) and effects on BHP enrollment/payments (affecting ~2,000 individuals and reducing Federal spending by ~$17 million in 2027). Estimates rely on internal FFE data and MIDAS analyses. HHS seeks comment on estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of APTC for individuals ineligible for Medicaid due to immigration status and with income <100% FPL (§155.305(f)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Disallow APTC for people who are ineligible for Medicaid because of immigration status and who have household income below 100% of the FPL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimates one-time eligibility system update costs of $4,316,278 in PY 2026 and an annual reduction in information collection burden of $24,126,144 beginning 2026. Using 237,125 affected enrollees and average monthly APTC $656.89, estimates annual APTC savings of $1,869,180,495 beginning PY 2026. Discusses projected BHP enrollment/payment assumptions and seeks comments on impact estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure To File and Reconcile (FTR) policy change to 1‑tax‑year FTR (§155.305(f)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend paragraph so that in PY 2028 and beyond all Exchanges may not determine a tax filer or their enrollee eligible for APTC if HHS notifies the Exchange that APTC were paid for a year where the filer did not file a Federal tax return and reconcile APTC (a 1‑tax‑year FTR process). Exchanges may optionally adopt earlier in PY 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes notice language changes to convey increased urgency. Estimates system development costs: approximately 10,000 hours per Exchange in 2026 (specific staff hour breakdowns and hourly rates provided); aggregate State Exchanges one-time burden estimated at 200,000 hours costing $19,399,000 and Federal Government 10,000 hours costing $969,950 (total 210,000 hours, $20,368,950). Estimates APTC savings and enrollment reductions (e.g., households losing APTC could be approx. 28,500 with ~$179 million annual savings based on 8 months of enrollment and $784 per month APTC removed). Seeks comment on impact estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income verification when trusted data sources indicate income <100% FPL (§155.320(c)(3)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend to indefinitely extend the requirement for applicants to submit documentation when they attest to income qualifying as applicable taxpayer but trusted data sources show income below 100% FPL starting in 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimates increased burden costs: ~$20.2M for Federal platform Exchanges and $12.4M for State Exchanges starting 2027, one-time system update costs ($775,960 Federal platform; ~$16.3M State Exchanges in 2026), and ~$13.7M annual consumer burden for documentation starting 2027. Projects reductions in people receiving APTC (50,000 Federal platform; 31,000 State Exchanges) and annual APTC expenditure reductions of ~ $213M for the maintained policy. Recognizes burden on State Exchanges and requests comments to inform decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income verification when tax data unavailable (§155.320(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose removal of §155.320(c)(5) that allowed Exchanges to continue the income verification process when IRS was contacted but returned no data (instead of accepting attestation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimates large increases in annual burden costs starting 2027: ~$102.3M (Federal platform) and ~$62.8M (State Exchanges) for receiving, reviewing, verifying documents and outreach; one-time system updates ~$872,955 (Federal platform) and ~$18.3M (State Exchanges) in 2026; increased annual consumer burden ~$69.48M to submit documentation. Projects reduction in APTC: potentially to zero for 252,000 Federal platform enrollees and 155,000 State Exchange enrollees, yielding estimated annual APTC reduction of ~$1,069M (using 4 months average reduction). Solicits comments on assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend removal (permanent prohibition) of the 150% FPL Special Enrollment Period (§155.420)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to no longer 'sunset' the prohibition on Exchanges offering the 150% FPL SEP, aligning with legislation that prohibits APTC for plans enrolled through that SEP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes if SEP were restored it would increase adverse selection; therefore removing it reduces premiums by estimated 3–4% and decreases APTC expenditures by $3.4–$4.5B per year (RIA uses $3.8B). Seeks comment on impact estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑enrollment SEP verification requirement for Federal Platform (§155.420(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow Federal Platform Exchanges to continue pre-enrollment verification for SEPs other than Loss of Minimum Essential Coverage and require pre-enrollment verification for at least 75% of new enrollments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipated program integrity benefits (reduced improper subsidy payments) but possible deterrence among younger enrollees. Estimates reduced premiums by ~0.5–1.0% and maintained APTC spending reduction of ~$105.4M. Estimates increased processing/pending enrollments: ~293,073 additional pended enrollments annually, increased consumer cost ~$7.33M beginning 2027, increased ongoing processing cost ~$11.7M annually (293,073 x $40 per SVI), and increased annual labor burden cost ~$2.9M. Seeks comments on impact estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expansion of hardship exemption eligibility to include those ineligible for APTC/CSRs due to projected income (§155.605(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend to codify/expand hardship exemption eligibility to individuals who are ineligible for APTC or CSRs due to projected household income (below 100% or above 250% FPL), enabling qualification for catastrophic coverage under section 1302(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes most States delegate processing to HHS; four State Exchanges process their own exemptions and would see administrative burden. Estimates manual processing takes ~19 minutes per application with adjusted hourly wage $49.52, per-application cost $15.75. Estimates ~1,072 applications annually for the four States and total annual cost ~$16,884. Discusses possibility and estimated one‑time costs of automating exemption processing (detailed staff-hours and cost breakdown totaling ~$160,790 per State; ~$643,160 for four States) and variability depending on State systems. Seeks comment on burden estimates, application time, and automation opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification of Exchange network adequacy standards (§155.1050)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend §155.1050(a)(2) to eliminate federal requirements that State Exchanges/SBE-FPs establish quantitative time-and-distance network adequacy standards at least as stringent as FFE standards and to no longer require quantitative network adequacy reviews prior to certifying QHPs; instead require State Exchanges/SBE-FPs to ensure QHPs provide sufficient access meeting applicable standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: many States have robust standards and are better positioned to evaluate local networks. Anticipated to maintain regulatory burden for 22 State Exchanges and 1 SBE-FP and provide flexibility; estimated impact $1,560,780 beginning PY 2027. Notes potential increased administrative burden on multi‑state issuers and unknown consumer impacts with risk of decreased access if State standards are less protective. Seeks comment on impact estimates and assumptions.
